newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK unemployment, earnings data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK unemployment, earnings data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to data showing UK unemployment fell 18,400 in May to give a jobless rate of 5.8 percent, while average earnings rose an underlying 4.5 percent in the three months to April and April unit wage costs were up 2.2 percent.

"I still suspect there may be some influence here from the Jobseekers' Allowance. It is a smaller unemployment number, I would have expected something closer to 40,000, so perhaps some sign that the speed of the fall is slowing."

"But we're still down to 5.8 percent and this is quite a low level by UK standards. More importantly, average earnings have not increased. But I still feel that in the months to come the service sector is going to be the key area. We're still seeing wage pressures here and this will eventually feed through into the underlying series."

"The smaller than expected monthly decline in unemployment should help to allay some fears about the labour market tightening. Next month markets will be looking for a decline in average earnings growth to below 4.5 percent."

"Smaller than expected decline in joblessness and some positive news on inflation which should support the UK interest rate markets and may be a small negative for the pound...The data have been very unreliable in recent months and we would not take this as any indication that the economy is slowing down. Average earnings were unchanged at 4.5 percent. However, there were downward revisions to the production and manufacturing sectors...This was sufficient to pull unit labour costs down to 2.2 percent. This should tend to dampen immediate concerns about the need for further monetary tightening."
